title: Partnership accounts
examples: How do I calculate the interest on capital for the appropriation account?
What is the difference between the capital account and the current account?
When do I prepare the appropriation account in the partnership books?

explain.say: Today we are learning about appropriation accounts in partnerships.

items: Includes: Interest on capital, salary, etc.

explain.say: The appropriation account shows how profits are divided among partners.
Interest on capital is usually calculated on the opening capital balance.
The current account records yearly changes, keeping capital separate.
The partnership deed dictates how profits are actually shared between partners.
In real life, a small business uses this to pay partners fairly.

faq.q: What is the main purpose of preparing an appropriation account?
faq.a: It shows how the total net profit is divided among the partners according to the partnership agreement. It helps ensure all partners receive their agreed share.
asks: Why do we need to show profit distribution?
What does the appropriation account calculate?

faq.q: How is interest on capital calculated?
faq.a: It is calculated by multiplying the partner's opening capital balance by the agreed interest rate. This amount is then shown in the appropriation account.
asks: Do I use the closing capital for interest?
What is the formula for interest on capital?

faq.q: What is the difference between the capital and current accounts?
faq.a: The capital account shows the permanent investment, while the current account handles temporary changes like annual profits and drawings. This keeps records clearer.
asks: When should I use the current account?

faq.q: Does the partnership deed always tell us how to distribute profits?
faq.a: Yes, the partnership deed is the primary source for profit sharing rules. If there is no deed, the law usually dictates the sharing method.
asks: What if there is no partnership deed?
Is the deed always the final word?

faq.q: Do drawings affect the appropriation account?
faq.a: Drawings are usually recorded in the current account, but the profit share derived from the appropriation account is what ultimately affects the capital structure.
asks: Is drawing a deduction from profit?

facts: The appropriation account distributes net profit among partners.
Interest on capital is usually calculated on the opening capital.
The current account records fluctuations, separating them from the fixed capital.
The partnership deed governs the method of profit sharing.

quiz.say: If a partner's salary is paid, where is this amount recorded?

options.show: As a deduction from the profit and loss account.
options.say: As a deduction from the profit and loss account.

quiz.why: The appropriation account is specifically designed to show all items that reduce or distribute the net profit, including partner salaries.

wrong.0: All distributions must first pass through the appropriation account for proper accounting treatment.
wrong.1: The profit and loss account determines the net profit; the appropriation account distributes that already calculated net profit.
wrong.3: The capital account represents the permanent investment and is not used for annual profit distribution items like salaries.

quiz.say: If the partnership agreement is silent on interest, what is the general rule?

options.show: No interest on capital is provided.
options.say: No interest on capital is provided.

options.show: Interest is calculated on the average capital.
options.say: Interest is calculated on the average capital.

options.show: Interest is calculated on the closing capital.
options.say: Interest is calculated on the closing capital.

options.show: Interest is paid only if the profit is high.
options.say: Interest is paid only if the profit is high.

quiz.why: Unless the partnership deed specifies otherwise, no partner is entitled to interest on their capital.

wrong.1: Averaging capital is not the standard method unless specifically directed by the deed.
wrong.2: Interest is typically calculated on the opening balance as the starting point for the period.
wrong.3: The right to interest is usually based on the agreement, not solely on the level of profitability.

quiz.say: When recording annual drawings, which account is primarily affected?
quiz.why: Drawings represent temporary withdrawals of capital during the year, which are recorded in the current account, not the main capital account.

wrong.0: The appropriation account deals with profit distribution, not the recording of partner withdrawals.
wrong.1: The P&L account determines the profit before distribution; drawings are a separate transaction.
wrong.2: The current account acts as the intermediary record before the final balance sheet figures are set.
